form_analysis.feedback: Comprehensive aftercare form for laser skin tag removal with clear guidance on the minimal healing process. Good emphasis on monitoring for regrowth and addressing underlying causes.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare is for laser removal of skin tags (acrochordons). Laser vaporizes the stalk/base of the tag. Minimal downtime but requires specific care to prevent infection and regrowth.

instructions.general_directive: Follow for 3-7 days of simple wound care. Skin tag removal is generally straightforward with minimal complications.

sections.title: Laser Skin Tag Mechanism
sections.content: CO₂ laser precisely vaporizes skin tag at base. The tag may either immediately fall off or darken and fall off within days.

sections.title: Immediate Post-Laser Response
items: Small wound at base where tag was attached.
Tag may remain attached but darkened before falling off.

sections.title: Wound Care Protocol
items: Small bandage if in friction area (neck, underarms).
Antibiotic ointment optional for first 2-3 days.
DO NOT PICK at base if scab forms.

sections.title: Regrowth Monitoring
sections.content: Skin tags may regrow if base not completely removed. Monitor for: 1) Return of small bump at site 2) New tags in same area. Report regrowth for possible re-treatment.

sections.title: Underlying Cause Management
sections.content: Skin tags associated with: 1) Insulin resistance/diabetes 2) Hormonal changes 3) Friction 4) Genetics. Address underlying causes to prevent new tags: Weight management, friction reduction, blood sugar control.

sections.title: Multiple Tags Considerations
items: Multiple sessions may be needed for numerous tags.
Some insurance may cover if medically necessary.

sections.title: Realistic Expectations
items: Minimal scarring if proper care followed.
New tags may develop elsewhere over time.
